states.q: Compare the three quotes for the September show stand and recommend one.
states.answer:
After comparing, I recommend the Atelier Morel quote: it’s the most expensive of the three (€18,400 excl. VAT), but the only one that includes setup, lighting and insurance.
Studio Nord offers €15,900 excl. VAT, without lighting: adding €2,100 of spotlight rental brings the gap down to €400.
The Expo Plus quote (€13,200 excl. VAT) is still the cheapest, but delivery is planned the day before opening: too tight to set up the stand calmly.

Weigh the delay risk against the price gap

long.q: Write a full decision memo on the supplier choice, for management.
long.title: Decision memo · stand supplier
long.note: This point was checked against the signable quotes received on June 2; amounts are excluding VAT and team travel costs.
sections: The show runs September 11–15, hall 5. The 36 m² stand is a corner spot, with two sides open onto the main aisle.
Total price at equal scope, delivery date, lighting quality, possible reuse of the frame and cancellation terms.
All-inclusive quote at €18,400 excl. VAT. Modular aluminium frame, built-in LED lighting, insurance and setup in 6 hours by two technicians.
€15,900 excl. VAT without lighting. Custom wooden frame, very polished, but not reusable. Delivery guaranteed three days before opening.
€13,200 excl. VAT, lighting and furniture optional for €3,400. Delivery planned the evening of September 10, with no margin for delay.
Atelier Morel refunds 80% up to 30 days before. Studio Nord bills the design regardless. Expo Plus refunds nothing after signing.
The main risk is logistics: a day-before delivery forces an overnight setup, with €1,200 of extra labour.
Atelier Morel, for a calm setup and reuse of the frame at the Lyon show in February.
Approve the quote before June 15 to lock in the 30% deposit, then send the stand plan to the supplier.

deep.q: Do deep research on the handmade ceramics market in France, to prepare the Lyon opening.
plan: Size and growth of the handmade ceramics market in France (2023–2026)
Buyer profiles: individuals, hospitality, concept stores
Sales channels: trade shows, shops, online
Average prices by type of piece
Main players and Atelier Morel’s positioning
body: The French handmade ceramics market reached €410 million in 2025, up 7% a year since 2023. Demand is driven by hospitality and concept stores.
With 38,000 fine-craft businesses, ceramics is nearly 11% of the sector; workshops of fewer than 5 people make up most of it.
Individuals aged 30 to 50 remain the core customers, but professional purchases grow twice as fast.
Trade shows remain the first acquisition channel for 61% of workshops; online sales now exceed 30% of established brands’ revenue.
The average handmade plate sells for €38 and a large platter for €120, with a 1-to-3 spread depending on reputation.
About ten houses shape the high end; Atelier Morel stands out with limited runs and short lead times.
Open the Lyon shop with a visible workshop, strengthen presence at two trade shows and launch an offer for hospitality.
